chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'So they were not submissive to their Lord, nor were they humbling themselves.' He said: 'Submission (al-istikana) is yielding (humility), and humbling oneself (at-tadarru') is raising the hands and beseeching with them both.'

key_terms.الاسْتِكَانَةُ: Submission or yielding (a state of humility)
key_terms.رَفْعُ الْيَدَيْنِ: Raising the hands (a ritual gesture in supplication)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between istikana and tadarru in Quranic exegesis?
ai.summary: In this exegetical narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the distinction between 'istikana' as an internal state of yielding and 'tadarru' as the physical manifestation of raising hands is clarified, linking linguistic precision to ritual practice. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for defining the specific bodily movements associated with humble supplication, emphasizing that true devotion combines inner humility with outward physical expression. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the unity of heart and body in acts of worship, where physical gestures like raising hands are not merely symbolic but integral to the concept of 'tadarru'.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [23:76] but they were not submissive to their Lord, nor were they humbling themselves. So heasws said: ‘The submission, it is the yielding, and the humbleness, it is the raising of the hands and the beseeching with them both’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Once I asked abu Ja’far (a.s.) about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ‘. . . but they did not ‘Istakanu (submit themselves to their Lord,) nor did they make themselves humble ( yatadarra’un ).’ [23:76]
The Imam said, ’’Al-Tstikana, means humility and al- tadarru’ means raising both hands and begging for help from (Allah) with both hands.’”
